summary:
P1.5 first slice: fewer JSDoc/TypeScript errors in the app, with no behaviour change.
- EntityMentionTextarea.jsx: reworded the header comment so '@-mentions' isn't parsed as a JSDoc tag, and added a props typedef with campaignId, placeholder, rows and className optional. This clears about 25 'campaignId is missing' errors at call sites.
- EntityMentionRenderer.jsx: typed the props so className is optional, and typed the inner mention component to accept entityId.
- .gmos/tasks.json: P1.5 note records 729 -> 698 errors.
Only comments and JSDoc changed, so there are no runtime changes and no changelog entry (internal).
Verification: the app typecheck ratchet reports 698 errors (baseline 729). Lint, check:repo, build and the 5 src test suites (16 tests) pass, and gmos-qa gave PASS on both steps.
Baseline: .typecheck-baseline stays at 729 on purpose, because the user said not to edit it. The owner can lock in 698 later with 'npm run typecheck:baseline'.
Known local-only issue: on this Windows checkout (core.autocrlf=true, so CRLF working files), scripts/scripts.test.mjs fails to load in Vitest with a SyntaxError on the shebang scripts it imports. Git stores those files with LF and CI runs on Linux, so CI is unaffected. None of those files were touched in this mission.
Follow-up: autoFocus is passed to EntityMentionTextarea at SessionNotesPanel:138 and CampaignNotes:81 but never forwarded. That leaves 2 TS2322 errors, kept for a later slice because fixing them would change behaviour.
needs_user: none. Risky: no (no migrations, auth, billing, CI, dependencies or pipeline scripts touched).
